title: Pseudo-Palindromic Paths in a Binary Tree
statement: Each node of the binary tree `root` stores a digit from 1 to 9. Consider every path that starts at the root and goes down to a leaf (a node with no children). Such a path is **pseudo-palindromic** when its values, taken as a multiset, can be arranged in some order that reads the same forwards and backwards. Return how many root-to-leaf paths are pseudo-palindromic.
constraints: The tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes
notes:
## Intuition

A list of values can be rearranged into a palindrome exactly when at most one value occurs an odd number of times (that one, if any, goes in the middle). So along a path we only need each digit's count **parity**, not the count itself. Nine parities fit in the bits of one integer: toggling bit `val` each time a digit appears keeps the odd digits as set bits. The brute force, which copies every path and counts its digits, is slower and uses more memory on deep trees.

## Approach

1. Run `dfs(node, parity)` from the root with `parity = 0` (no digits seen).
2. A missing child contributes no paths, so return 0.
3. Flip bit `node.val` to get `mask`, the parities including this node.
4. At a leaf, the path qualifies when `mask` has at most one set bit; `mask & (mask - 1)` clears the lowest set bit, so it is 0 exactly then.
5. Otherwise return the sum of the counts from both children.

## Example 1, step by step

`root = [2,3,1,3,1,null,1]`. At the root, `mask = 1 << 2 = 0b100`. Going left to 3 gives `0b1100`; its leaf child 3 flips bit 3 back to `0b100` (one bit set, counts 1), and its leaf child 1 gives `0b1110` (three bits, counts 0). Going right to 1 gives `0b110`, and its leaf child 1 gives `0b100` (counts 1). The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each node is visited once with O(1) work.
- Space: O(h) for the recursion, where `h` is the tree's height.

## Pitfalls

- Only count at real leaves; a node with one child is not the end of a path.
- Use XOR to toggle parity; adding counts and checking later needs a full array per path.
- `mask & (mask - 1)` must be compared with 0 inside parentheses, because `===` binds tighter than `&`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dfs(node, parity)` | number of qualifying paths through `node`, given the parities above it |
| `parity` | bit `d` is set when digit `d` occurred an odd number of times above `node` |
| `mask` | `parity` after including `node.val` |

narration.2: dfs counts the qualifying root-to-leaf paths below node, given the digit parities on the path above it.
narration.3: A missing child ends no path...
narration.6: Toggle this digit's bit: a set bit means the digit has appeared an odd number of times.
narration.7: No children: this node ends a root-to-leaf path.
narration.8: The path can form a palindrome when at most one bit is set, which mask & (mask - 1) tests.
narration.10: Otherwise add the qualifying paths found through each child.
narration.12: Start at the root with every parity even.
